topic: Speed beats polish when winning clients
caption:
Nobody hires the agency with the best deck.

I have lost pitches with better slides.
I have won pitches with no slides at all.

The difference was nearly always the same thing.
Who picked up the phone first.

A business owner with a burst pipe, a lawsuit or a dead website does not compare decks.
They call three people.
They hire the one who answers.

So we answer in minutes, not days.
It has won us more clients than any proposal.

#SmallBusiness #Marketing
alt: Quote card from Mohd Farhan: Nobody hires the agency with the best deck. They hire the one that called back first.

topic: Speed beats polish when winning clients
caption:
Most ad accounts do not need more budget.

They need fewer keywords.

The pattern I see every week:
Results drop, so the owner raises the budget.
The extra money goes to the same broad terms that were already failing.
Cost per lead goes up, not down.

What works is the opposite.
Cut the account back to the 20 terms that bring in buyers.
Block everything else.
Then add budget.

Less coverage. More customers.

#GoogleAds #PPC
alt: Quote card from Nasir Ahmad: Most ad accounts do not need more budget. They need fewer keywords.

topic: Speed to lead, Harvard Business Review
caption:
23% of US firms never replied to a web enquiry at all.

Harvard Business Review sent enquiries to 2,241 companies.
37% replied within an hour.
16% took 1 to 24 hours.
24% took longer than a day.
23% never answered.

Most businesses think they have a lead problem.
A lot of them have a reply problem.

Before you spend another dollar on ads, test it yourself.
Fill in your own contact form and time how long the reply takes.

Source: HBR, "The Short Life of Online Sales Leads", 2011.

#LeadGeneration #Sales
alt: Chart: of 2,241 US firms sent a web enquiry, 37% replied within an hour, 16% in 1 to 24 hours, 24% after a day and 23% never replied.

topic: Speed to lead, Harvard Business Review
caption:
42 hours.

That was the average time a US firm took to reply to a web lead in the Harvard Business Review study.

Calling within an hour made a firm 7 times more likely to qualify the lead than calling an hour later.
Compared with waiting 24 hours or more, it was 60 times more likely.

I see this inside ad accounts all the time.
The cost per lead looks fine.
The leads go cold in an inbox nobody checks.

The fastest fix in paid ads is often not in the ads.

Source: HBR, 2011, 2,241 US firms.

#SpeedToLead #GoogleAds
alt: Graphic: US firms took 42 hours on average to reply to a web lead. Calling within an hour made qualifying the lead 7 times more likely.

caption:
The 3 stages of hiring a $300 SEO agency.

Stage 1: this is a bargain.
Stage 2: month 4, still no calls.
Stage 3: why is my site on a casino blog?

Cheap SEO is rarely cheap.
Bad links can take months to clean up.

Before you sign, ask to see exactly which links they will build.

#SEO #SmallBusiness
alt: Three-panel meme: the 3 stages of hiring a $300 SEO agency, from "this is a bargain" to "why is my site on a casino blog?"

caption:
The 3 stages of switching on Performance Max.

Stage 1: Google says it finds new customers.
Stage 2: where did 40% of the budget go?
Stage 3: new lead, "asdf asdf".

Performance Max can work.
For a local lead business, check the placement report and switch on spam protection on your forms before you trust it.

#PerformanceMax #GoogleAds
alt: Three-panel meme: the 3 stages of switching on Performance Max, ending with a spam lead that reads "asdf asdf".

topic: AI cannot run your ad budget
caption:
"We do not need an agency. ChatGPT can run our Google Ads."

ChatGPT can write the ads.
It cannot see that half the budget is going to job seekers.
It cannot hear that the leads are bad on the phone.
It cannot tell you that your best customers search a word you never bid on.

Use AI to work faster.
Do not let it decide where the money goes.

#AI #GoogleAds
alt: Tweet-style card with a cartoon dog sitting calmly in a burning room, captioned as the ad account three weeks after ChatGPT took over.

topic: AI cannot run your ad budget
caption:
"Just accept every Google recommendation. They know best."

Some of them are good.
Many of them raise your budget, broaden your keywords or switch your bidding to something you never chose.

Here is how I sort them:
Fix errors: yes.
Add assets: usually yes.
Raise budget, broad match, auto-apply: look first.

A recommendation is advice from the company that sells the clicks.

#GoogleAds #PPC
alt: Tweet-style card with a flying stack of cash, captioned as the daily budget after accepting every Google recommendation.

topic: AI will not find you without SEO / search terms report
caption:
"We don't need SEO. AI will just find us."

I hear this every week now.

So try it.
Open ChatGPT and ask for the best plumber, dentist or roofer in your town.

The names it gives you come from your Google profile, your reviews and what other sites say about you.
Those are the same things SEO has always worked on.

AI did not replace SEO.
It made the gap between found and invisible bigger.

#SEO #AIsearch
alt: Crayon comic: an owner says AI will find them, then sees ChatGPT recommend three other plumbers.

topic: Real Google Ads results with DM ask
caption:
$94.4K in. $691K back.

One Google Ads account from August 2023 to August 2025.
$4.12 cost per conversion.
732% return on ad spend.

No secret tool.
Tight keywords, real conversion tracking, and weekly search term cleaning for two years.

The client name stays private.
The setup does not.

DM me "SAUCE" and I will send you the campaign structure we used.

#GoogleAds #PPC
alt: Google Ads screenshot: $94.4K cost, 691K conversion value, 732% return on ad spend, August 2023 to August 2025.

topic: AI will not find you without SEO / search terms report
caption:
"My Google Ads are fine."

Then I open the search terms report.

Plumber jobs.
Free plumbing advice.
How to unclog a drain yourself.

Every one of those clicks was paid for.
None of those people were ever going to hire a plumber.

The campaign view tells you how the account is doing.
The search terms tell you what you actually bought.
Read them every week.

#GoogleAds #PPC
alt: Crayon comic: an owner says his Google Ads are fine, then sees money spent on searches like plumber jobs and free advice.

caption:
Never seen a better example of user behaviour.

Someone built a path.
People walked straight across the grass instead.

Websites work the same way.
Visitors ignore your menu and look for the phone number, the price and the reviews.

If those are hard to find, they make their own path.
It usually leads back to Google.

#UX #WebDesign
alt: Photo of a dirt path worn across a field toward apartment buildings, next to the paved route nobody used.

topic: Real Google Ads results with DM ask
caption:
$3.4K spent in 14 days.
$26.4K back.
777% return on ad spend.

Nothing clever happened in this account.
We cut the keyword list hard, blocked the junk searches and let the budget sit on what was already selling.

Screenshot from the account, 6 to 19 August 2025.

DM me "setup" and I will send you the keyword list structure.

#GoogleAds #ROAS

topic: Surprises lose clients / the word free
caption:
Clients do not fire agencies for bad months.

They fire them for surprises.

A bad month with a phone call on day 3 builds trust.
A bad month the client finds in a report on day 30 ends the contract.

Every agency has bad months.
The ones that keep clients tell them first.

#AgencyLife #ClientService
alt: Tweet-style card from Mohd Farhan: Clients do not fire agencies for bad months. They fire them for surprises.

caption:
Twenty buttons.

One of them is worn black.

A heatmap of a service website looks just like this.
Most people click the same one thing.
Usually it is the phone number.

So make that button big, keep it at the top, and stop giving the other nineteen the same weight.

#Heatmap #CRO
alt: Photo of an old apartment intercom panel where one button out of twenty is worn black from use.

caption:
More traffic will not fix a leaking website.

Slow page.
No phone number in sight.
A form with 11 fields.

Each one loses people you already paid to bring in.

We check the holes before we touch the ad budget.
It is the cheapest growth most small businesses have.

#ConversionRate #CRO
alt: Animation: visitors fall into a funnel and leak out through a slow page, a missing phone number and a long form, so few become calls.

topic: Surprises lose clients / the word free
caption:
Every Google Ads account I open has the same search term in it.

"Free."

Free quote is fine.
Free advice, free course and free download are not.

It takes about 4 minutes to add "free" with exceptions to your negative keyword list.
It is usually the cheapest saving in the account.

#GoogleAds #NegativeKeywords
alt: Tweet-style card from Nasir Ahmad: Every Google Ads account I open has the same search term in it. It is the word free.

caption:
This is what one week of clicks really bought.

Eight search terms.
Four were people looking for jobs, free tips or salaries.
In this example, $216 of the $396 went to people who would never buy.

You fix it in the search terms report.
Mark the bad terms as negatives.
Do it every week, not once.

Example account, illustrative numbers.

#GoogleAds #PPC
alt: Animation: eight search terms appear with their cost, and four junk terms like plumber salary get struck out as negatives.
